subject: Clarify tax & pass-through language on Marketplace order form
messages:
From: Dana Lopez <dana@cloudsail.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: accounts-payable@cloudsail.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify tax treatment on Marketplace order form

Hi Connor,

Quick one from our finance team as we prep the reseller addendum: the marketplace order form references a "pass-through taxes" paragraph but it's not clear whether CloudSail will be listed as the ultimate fee payer for local indirect taxes (VAT/GST) when we resell to our customers. Our AP team needs a short note and any supporting evidence that Redwood will accept invoice passthrough (or details on how tax will be invoiced) so we can map it to our accounting flows.

Can you confirm: 
- Whether Redwood will include reseller-facing VAT on Redwood invoices when billing via marketplace?
- If not, what customer-level tax responsibility language we should expect?

We need this clarified before legal approves the order form. Attaching the AP checklist.

Thanks,
Dana
Dana Lopez
Director, Finance Operations | CloudSail, Inc.
attachments: AP-Checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Dana Lopez <dana@cloudsail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify tax treatment on Marketplace order form

Dana — thanks for the note and for including the AP checklist. Short answer: Redwood's marketplace flows vary by channel and region, so there are two common patterns depending on the marketplace (direct listing vs. intermediary):

1) Redwood invoices CloudSail (reseller) and includes applicable indirect taxes on that invoice when Redwood is the seller of record. In that case Redwood collects VAT/GST and remits per our local tax obligations.

2) For reseller/intermediated models where the cloud marketplace is the billing intermediary, the marketplace often invoices the end-customer directly and the reseller (CloudSail) is responsible for ensuring tax treatment on your resale. In those flows Redwood's order form will include a pass-through clause that shifts tax responsibility to the reseller where the reseller is the seller of record.

Action items I can take now: 
- Attach precedent tax evidence we provide to partners (I have a zipped bundle with sample invoices and our tax registration summaries).
- Loop in Legal (Laura) to propose a short, unambiguous order form clause that states when Redwood is seller of record vs when reseller is responsible for taxes.

I attached the evidence bundle and a quick outline of suggested language. If you can share which marketplace (AWS/GCP/CloudMart) is in play I will pull the exact flow.

Connor O'Brien
Partner Sales | Redwood Inference
Attachments: cloudsail_tax_evidence.zip (zip)

Hi Dana and Connor,

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the current order form language and attached a redline that focuses on two things: (a) explicitly stating the "seller of record" determination will be driven by the specific marketplace listing and (b) providing a short, mandatory notification process so Redwood or the reseller provides a tax invoice within X days of charge for reconciliation.

Suggested short clause (for your review):
"Tax Treatment and Resale. Seller of Record: The party designated in the applicable marketplace listing or order confirmation shall be the "seller of record" for purposes of indirect taxes (VAT, GST, sales tax). If Redwood is the seller of record, Redwood will collect and remit applicable indirect taxes and will include those taxes on invoices to the reseller. If the reseller or marketplace is the seller of record, the reseller shall be responsible for any indirect taxes due in connection with resold services. Either party must provide tax documentation or an invoice reflecting taxes within 15 days of a written request for reconciliation."

Please see redlined_orderform_v2.docx attached. A couple of notes: 
- We should avoid language that forces full indemnities tied to tax claims (operations teams hate the cascade). Keep responsibility to payment and cooperation for reconciliation.
- If CloudSail needs a certificate of Redwood's VAT registration in specific countries we can include a schedule of registrations, but that will add time.

Connor — once Dana confirms which marketplace and whether CloudSail expects Redwood to be seller of record, we can finalize the clause and get the order form signed.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
